newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says Kashmir key to any talks with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says Kashmir key to any talks with India.

text.p: Pakistan on Friday said Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deva Gowda's offer for talks was useless unless they seek to resolve their rival claims to Kashmir.

"Kashmir is the core issue between the two countries and without a meaningful negotiation on the core issue, discussion on peripheral issues will not help improve the situation," the domestic APP news agency quoted a Foreign Ministry spokesman as saying.
Deve Gowda told Indian troops during a visit on Thursday to the part of Kashmir that New Delhi controls that he favoured resuming peace talks with Pakistan.
But he said India would never give up its share of the disputed Himalayan region.
"So far as the Kashmir issue is concerned, it is a closed chapter," Deve Gowda said. "Jammu and Kashmir is a part and parcel of India, and there is no question of its compromise."
India rules two-thirds and Pakistan the rest of Kashmir, over which they fought two wars after independence from Britain in 1947.
Islamabad wants predominantly Moslem Kashmir to vote on whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India, which regards all of Kashmir part of India.
India also accuses Pakistan of arming and training militants fighting Indian rule. Pakistan says it gives the rebels only moral and political support.
